stem.text: The amount of oil in a holding tank changes at the rate \( A'(t) = 10 \cos{\left(\frac{\pi t}{5} \right)} + 1 \) barrels per hour for \( 0 \le t \le 10 \). At time \( t = 0 \) there are 180 barrels of oil in the tank, and t is measured in hours. Using a calculator, find the time in \( 0 \le t \le 10 \) at which the amount A(t) of oil is greatest, and justify the answer. Show the setup for the calculations.

answer_key.label: The amount is greatest at t = 2.659, where A is 198.495 barrels, the largest of the values of A at t = 0, at both critical points and at t = 10.

worked_solution.text: The amount is \( A(t) = 180 + \int_{0}^{t} \left(10 \cos{\left(\frac{\pi s}{5} \right)} + 1\right)\,ds \), so \( A'(t) = 10 \cos{\left(\frac{\pi t}{5} \right)} + 1 \). Setting \( A'(t) = 0 \) and solving with a calculator gives \( t = 2.659 \) and \( t = 7.341 \) in the interval.
worked_solution.rule_named: critical points of an accumulation function

worked_solution.text: The candidates are the critical points and both endpoints: \( A(0) = 180 \), \( A(2.659) \approx 198.495 \), \( A(7.341) \approx 171.505 \), and \( A(10) = 180 + \int_{0}^{10} A'(s)\,ds = 190 \).
The largest candidate value is about 198.495, at the first critical point, so the amount is greatest at \( t = 2.659 \) hours.

options.label: The amount is greatest at t = 10, where A is 190 barrels, because A' is positive on the interval from t = 7.341 to t = 10.
options.derivation: a local argument at the right end: A' is positive just before the endpoint, so A is taken to be greatest there
